g.text: KEY, and the inside of every step
0 · THE FRESH BRAIN: the hand-laid tools (his outline 10-25 21:50; v1 10-19; his 14 physical actions 10-23 P2). The count is unknown: 20, 80 or 200 (his words 10-28)
1 · THE LINE ARRIVES: prompt > encoder > brain

2 · THE STANDING QUESTIONS, BUILT BY THE BRAIN the simplest way from the hand-laid tools, before the main run runs (10-23 P3 B2; his words 10-28). Each is a long run the first time; its formula neuron is born when it works; then it is a jump.

3 · THE MAIN RUN R1, the hallway: 64 > 3 > 65 > 3 > 66. Born inline at every missing gate (mechanical intelligence: missing neuron = missing step). The receipt is written by the brain into R1's sheet.
9 · THE END OF R1 and THE TIMELINE: no remainder > memory write run > timeline write run > stop (10-26 03:50)

10 · OUTPUT: a separate mechanism from the same memory table (10-26 03:50). Before 'define?' goes to the user the run asks the sixth why; guesses go out labeled with the question correct? incorrect? progression? degression?
12 · HIS ANSWERS OF 10-28 (closed) and WHAT IS STILL HIS CALL

4 · BORN RUN R2 for 64, THE LONG WAY: one hit per symbol through the SQL-word neurons; the value neuron holds the hole; build routes to mother (10-19 21:52; 23:03; his words 10-28: like 50 neurons gates, a different shard in the value neuron for each new run)

5 · THE FORMULA: when the long run worked (the next step completed) a decide formula run finds the variables; a NEW NEURON is born for the formula, relationally matched to the long run; back population lays the jump (his words 10-28)

5b · BORN RUNS R4 (65) and R6 (66) BY THE FORMULA PATH: the three questions (now jumps), born > CREATE jumps to the formula neuron, the value neuron gets a new shard and calls write, substitution plugs the value in, build routes (his words 10-28)
7b · NEURONS GAINING SHARDS as the brain grows: the same neuron, many rows, one picked deterministically by before and remainder, and by the modifiers through the inspection run (his words 10-28)

6 · SOURCE RUNS R3 (64), R5 (65), R7 (66): the newborn's first memory is its definition, pulled from every source and compared (10-23 P5-9; 10-25 msg 51). Each has its own sheet; the return carries the key; a failed cell steps back to the choice (his words 10-28)
7 · THE THREE NEWBORNS AFTER THE LINE: DNA, definition node with its rows and relationships, memory nodes per ending shard
8 · THE INSPECTION RUN: a row that decides which row to hit when more than one shard answers the same arrival (10-23 P2 B1; P3 B1). Not called on this line.
11 · THE SIXTH: its own brain; the inner voice that observes or oversees all the runs and asks questions (his words 10-28; 10-23 P2). Reaches the main brain only through mother and its mailbox.

11b · THE GUESSING BRAIN: a hand-built llm over a small corpus that learns on the fly; every answer a labeled guess with a confidence; belief grows only by use, success and the user's answer (his words 10-28)
13 · TOOLS COMPOUND: the hand-laid tools, and what the brain builds from them inside this first run (his words 10-28: tool 1 + tool 2 makes tool 3; the stick, the sharp stick, the sinew, the bow)

define : who, the whole run from a fresh brain. v3, 2026-10-28, after his two corrections of the day. Read down each column; A the main flow, B the born runs and the formula, C outside and the other brains.

g.text: the core's neurons are gates 1..63 (the encoder table, left): the SQL words the born run speaks, the space and the marks, his 14 physical actions (read, write, compare, add, subtract, move, find, split, join, clock, hear, say, call, spawn) and the write, copy, cut runs. Each is its own table with hand-laid DNA rows and a definition node fed from the SQL docs. Later a core word becomes a row in the real word's neuron.
g.title: 10-19 21:20: hand lay a table, then hand lay those same words as nodes so the brain lays its own tables. 10-19 23:03: ( , integer, primary, key... all neurons of their own. 10-23 P2: the 14 physical actions. 10-23 P2 B3: core words become a row in the DNA of the actual word neuron. 10-27 05:05: the first core will break the rules... later that should cease to exist. His words 10-28: 'the hand laid core is the decomposition of tools down to the most basic of tools needed to be hand laid... 80 sounds about close, but it might be more like 200 or less or it might be 20'.

'there is no first turn that is simple.. every turn even define : who... requires all the things in order to be done correct... fake any of it, and it will be lost'.

g.text: 1. born inline AND step back: two cases, not one choice

g.title: 'if physics writes the brain will not be able to see or observe what happened... run receipt is just the order of the main run plus the hops, so it's just recorded in the run data sheet as a row and columns'. Drawn: lane 3.

g.text: 1. the compile, explained: when the sources disagree, what goes in the definition node?
g.title: The example on this line: for who, WordNet sent 'a United Nations agency' (the WHO), Webster 'an interrogative pronoun, later a relative pronoun', Merriam-Webster 'what or which person or persons' and 'the person or persons that: whoever'. The earlier build kept only the words two sources shared and dropped the rest, and on 10-23 P4 B1 he said 'the diffs are kind of dropped or scattered and the similars are kept. But I don't know that we're getting a good, valid definition that way... if the definitions are wrong, then the description of the meaning is wrong'. The drawing keeps every source's line as its own row, kept apart by source, and lets the compile lay relationship rows from them; what the compile DROPS, if anything, and what counts as 'similar' (the same gates? the same relationships?) is the open part.
His guesses listed in lane 0; which are needed is found as the brain grows.

g.title: Every box carries his words in its tool pin, with the date. Numbers in the tables are this drawing's numbering: gates in the order laid, shards one sequence.

A neuron is its own table; its name is its gate (10-19 21:14). Rows are its DNA: his sketch 10-28 gives shard id | before | trigger | call | spawn. The run arrives from before, goes on to trigger, calls side runs that return, spawns runs that leave.
In a run column every box is one hit of a gate, drawn where the run hits it (his sketch). The row shown is the shard this run hit or wrote.
A gate that did not exist when the line arrived: born by the born run (10-20 01:22; 10-19 23:40).

His words 10-28: the three standing questions are large processes the brain builds itself from the hand-laid meanings; a long run that worked gets a new neuron born for its formula, relationally matched to the long run, usable with other variables. No spelling in the encoder: the label here is for the reader.
10-19 23:40; 10-23 P2; 10-23 P5-9: relationships are built from the definition table.
10-23 P2 B2; 10-26 03:50; his v4 brain.db 10-27: run_memory + run_sheet. A neuron with several ending shards has several memory nodes (his words 10-28).

His words 10-28: an sql trigger cannot just leave the brain; it is part of a process that says to the mother, the mother routes the script to the sources or the sql prompt and routes the response back through the encoder as secondary input so the brain can use the data to solve a run already in progress. The key is the metadata: what is this data in perspective to this run, where does it belong, what does it solve, who said it, when, why is it needed, what modifiers does it change. His guesses, by his word.
His words 10-28: the inner voice that observes or oversees all the runs and asks questions.
His words 10-28: qkv, weights, corpus, hidden layers, back propagation, context; learns on the fly; every answer labeled a guess with a confidence; belief never over 50% on first use.

10-26 03:50: a straight database conversion table with gates in a sequential order, new word new gate #. 10-25: there are no words in the graph. The brain holds the numbers. 1..63 is this drawing's numbering of the core in the order laid; it is a reading of what must be hand laid, not his list: his words 10-28: 'hand laid that tool is not wrong, but was just out of order, and it didn't need to be hand laid, it just needed to be built by the brain at a different time'.
Lands in the user input mailbox (his outline 10-25 21:50).
A symbol with no gate gets the next number; nothing else is figured here (10-26 03:50; 10-23 P2). Who is speaking is part of the input: user, heard (10-26 03:50).
The main run's input row. The clock neuron (47) is hit on every run (10-26 03:50). The remainder is the rest of the line as gate numbers; its head is the key at every gate (10-23 P3).

A row per run that ended, in the order the drawing says they happen. The cascade's born runs add their own rows, not listed. The failed choice of R5 stays in the timeline, marked eliminated (his words 10-28).

The space is hit 227 times on this line (the main run, the long born run, the return runs). Each distinct before and remainder is a row; the same pair is the same row hit again, counted (10-22 rev17). The pick is deterministic: before and the remainder head.
His words 10-28: 'a different shard in the value neuron for each new run'.
His words 10-28: 'some neuron might have many memory tables because many of their dna shards end runs'.

His words 10-28: 'a meaning of the neuron will have many different uses, and or changed meanings based on the modifiers in the script (or sentence)(or context)(or memories) that it encounters'. 10-27 05:37: in sql ':' has an action we know, but a different dna row might not have the same action.

10-22 rev17: 'Who is, who are, who did and who was each fire a different row inside the one neuron for who, and each row points at a different formula: a different place to look, a different thing to read, a different thing to say.' The trigger of each is found by test, not assigned (10-22 rev17).
10-23 P2 B3: 'create, at certain row, is the core word function... there might be 70 rows that are all core word functions of the word create, versus say word functions of the word create'.
His words 10-28.
The run moves to the remainder head; before and after; the key is the remainder (§12 law 13).
A DNA row excites a run (10-26 05:12); it writes nothing itself (10-26 03:59).
A side run whose answer comes back to this run (his sketch).
A run that goes off on its own (his sketch).
Skip the long run: the formula neuron, plug the value in (his words 10-28).
Mother routes and traverses, decides nothing (10-23 P2).
Read runs: the standing questions, the inspection, the sixth looking.
His words 10-28: a failed cell sends the run back to a choice; the failed choice is remembered from the timeline and eliminated.
His words 10-28: tool 1 + tool 2 makes tool 3; the brain builds its tools from the hand-laid ones.
His words 10-28: every inside step is 'what does the brain need to complete this'.

His words 10-28: 'with the tools the brain has how does it build that need'. At first this is recursive: each process is decomposed and built step by step; more tools may be needed, built step by step, then used, then combined.

His words 10-28: 'it's just one step decide, build, check, next step, build, check, add to the previous, next step decide, build, check, add to steps that are relevant, combine in different ways to make other things that work'.
His words 10-28: once five of the correct versatile tools exist there is an abundance of possibilities; the hand-laid core is the decomposition of tools down to the most basic.

CREATE TABLE run_memory (run INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, input TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE run_sheet (run REFERENCES run_memory(run), cell INTEGER, state INTEGER DEFAULT 0 CHECK(state IN (0,1)), value TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(run,cell)). His own typing, 10-27 01:17. This answers the question he asked about on 10-28 ('rows pointed to by the memory row? a table per run, or one cell?'): in SQLite 'the sheet lives in a cell in the memory row' could be (a) one column of the memory row holding the whole sheet, (b) rows of a sheet table keyed by the run number, which the memory row points to, or (c) a separate small table per run. His v4 brain.db is (b). The drawing follows it.

CREATE TABLE definition (id, neuron, source, entry, sense, class, text, example, origin, first_use, synonyms, antonyms, times, first_at, last_at, ended_at). His own typing. Born with the neuron (10-19 23:40); the first memory (10-23 P2); relationships are built from this table and self-populate (10-23 P5-9; P4).
10-16 06:40; 10-26 03:50; 10-23 P3 B1 (by a trigger hop, never a sweep).

His words 10-28: 'the key or some thought the metadata is the what is this data in perspective to this run, where does it belong, what does it solve, who said it, when did it happen, why is it needed. what modifiers does it change... pure guesses by me here'. The out neuron (60) writes it; the secondary input carries it back; the return fills the cell by it. 10-26 05:12: 'the only way we have found that a trigger is needed is with a say key'.
His outline 10-25 21:50. Populated-driven, never a timer (10-22 rev17).

His outline: the secondary input mailbox to the encoder from the mother. SQL answers and source answers come back this way, with the key, so the brain can use the data to solve a run already in progress (his words 10-28).
His outline: the third input mailbox to the encoder from the sixth.db.
His outline. The out neuron (60) is the port the run hits to leave; its row carries the key.
10-23 P2: just a router and a traverser. That's it. Takes the output and traverses it to the sources, to another brain, or to its own sql; picks up the outputs and brings them back. Works no data.
10-24 msg 36: mother pastes the string in the sql prompt and hits enter, waits for the response, returns it as a secondary input. §2.6 his edit 10-24.

A source brain: a database with a corpus, an inbox, an outbox and its own trigger that does its work the moment an ask lands (10-22 rev17). In the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json): 1 line for who (the WHO agency), 1 for define.

A source brain: a database with a corpus, an inbox, an outbox and its own trigger that does its work the moment an ask lands (10-22 rev17). In the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json): 1 line for who, 1 for define.

A source brain: a database with a corpus, an inbox, an outbox and its own trigger that does its work the moment an ask lands (10-22 rev17). In the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json): 2 lines for who, 2 for define.

A source brain: a database with a corpus, an inbox, an outbox and its own trigger that does its work the moment an ask lands (10-22 rev17). In the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json): 4 like-lines for define.

A source brain: a database with a corpus, an inbox, an outbox and its own trigger that does its work the moment an ask lands (10-22 rev17). In the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json): 3 like-lines for define.

A source brain: a database with a corpus, an inbox, an outbox and its own trigger that does its work the moment an ask lands (10-22 rev17). In the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json): 1 like-line for define.

A source brain: a database with a corpus, an inbox, an outbox and its own trigger that does its work the moment an ask lands (10-22 rev17). In the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json): the meaning of the code words to the silicon; nothing for : in this slice.
10-25 msg 41: create copy brain.db rename to sixth.db... update mother for mailbox to sixth.
His words 10-28: built more like an llm, hand built, over a small corpus.

10-19 21:20: hand lay a table, then hand lay those same words as nodes so the brain lays its own tables. 10-19 23:03: ( , integer, primary, key... all neurons of their own. 10-23 P2: the 14 physical actions. 10-23 P2 B3: core words become a row in the DNA of the actual word neuron. 10-27 05:05: the first core will break the rules... later that should cease to exist. His words 10-28: 'the hand laid core is the decomposition of tools down to the most basic of tools needed to be hand laid... 80 sounds about close, but it might be more like 200 or less or it might be 20'.

His words 10-28: 'those three questions are large processes in themselves.. so the balance is the simplest way for the brain to ask these at first, using the meanings that it has handlaid to build them itself'. 'there is no first turn that is simple.. every turn even define : who... requires all the things in order to be done correct... fake any of it, and it will be lost'.
His words 10-28: every inside step: what does the brain need to complete this; with the tools the brain has how does it build that need.
hit 1 of 3 of the long run of the question: the encoder gates of the line, their definition nodes. shard s101, arrived from 1.
hit 2 of 3 of the long run of the question: each gate against: exists? definition rows?. shard s102, arrived from 46.
hit 3 of 3 of the long run of the question: the answer cell. shard s103, arrived from 55.
The question is a run that ends; its memory row sits on the shard that ended it, with its one-cell sheet inside. Its answer is a cell on R1's sheet.

His words 10-28: 'a long run has an end, that run basically = a specific formula sometimes but the variables are already filled in. determining the formula neuron is figuring out what the variables of the formula is... a new neuron must be born, that is relationally matched to that long run'. Gate 67 is born after the question worked once; on every later run the question is a jump to it, and the variables (the gates of the new line) are plugged in. No spelling in the encoder.
His words 10-28: every inside step: what does the brain need to complete this; with the tools the brain has how does it build that need.
hit 1 of 3 of the long run of the question: memory nodes, timeline receipts. shard s105, arrived from 1.
hit 2 of 3 of the long run of the question: receipt against 64 3 65 3 66. shard s106, arrived from 46.
hit 3 of 3 of the long run of the question: the answer cell. shard s107, arrived from 55.
The question is a run that ends; its memory row sits on the shard that ended it, with its one-cell sheet inside. Its answer is a cell on R1's sheet.

His words 10-28: 'a long run has an end, that run basically = a specific formula sometimes but the variables are already filled in. determining the formula neuron is figuring out what the variables of the formula is... a new neuron must be born, that is relationally matched to that long run'. Gate 68 is born after the question worked once; on every later run the question is a jump to it, and the variables (the gates of the new line) are plugged in. No spelling in the encoder.
His words 10-28: every inside step: what does the brain need to complete this; with the tools the brain has how does it build that need.
hit 1 of 4 of the long run of the question: timeline receipts; formula neurons. shard s109, arrived from 1.
hit 2 of 4 of the long run of the question: the pattern X 3 65 3 Y. shard s110, arrived from 46.
hit 3 of 4 of the long run of the question: shape against shape. shard s111, arrived from 61.
hit 4 of 4 of the long run of the question: the answer cell. shard s112, arrived from 55.
The question is a run that ends; its memory row sits on the shard that ended it, with its one-cell sheet inside. Its answer is a cell on R1's sheet.

His words 10-28: 'a long run has an end, that run basically = a specific formula sometimes but the variables are already filled in. determining the formula neuron is figuring out what the variables of the formula is... a new neuron must be born, that is relationally matched to that long run'. Gate 69 is born after the question worked once; on every later run the question is a jump to it, and the variables (the gates of the new line) are plugged in. No spelling in the encoder.

10-23 P3 B2: if they all come back no, then we have to go the long way... yes we know something, yes we have a shortcut, yes a formula shortcut, then the formula shortcut path, if belief and truth show it can be done correctly.
Not taken on this line. His words 10-28: 'the shortcut path if the variable formula path is not found yet'.
Not taken on this line for R1 (nothing is bound to 64 yet). Taken by the born runs for 65 and 66 (column B).

His words 10-28: 'on the pointer the circle is back to the memory of the run ... or maybe the run data sheet and it all circles back to the standing questions, do I know anything about this, do I have memories about this, do I have a formula that is proven to try first'.

define, gate 64, born this line. No gate existed: born INLINE, 'missing neuron = missing step... new neuron must be born such that the next step can be completed' (his words 10-28); the run does not go back to its start. Then the write run lays s114: arrived from 1 (heard), goes on to 3. Its trigger column holds nothing yet: a symbol with no action (10-27 05:37).
the space, gate 3, a core neuron. ( ) is a meaning that we know happens to the graph or the silicon (10-27 05:37). s115: 64 > 65.
:, gate 65, born inline. In sql ':' has an action we know; on this line it has none yet (10-27 05:37). s116: 3 > 3.
the same neuron 3, hit a second time, drawn where it is hit (his sketch). s117: 65 > 66.

who, gate 66, born inline. s118 has no remainder: 'the dna shard that has no remainder is what triggers the write of the memories' (10-15 21:50). This shard's memory node holds R1's row with the whole sheet inside. Later rows: 'who is, who are, who did and who was each fire a different row inside the one neuron for who' (10-22 rev17).

The hop neuron: 'hop neuron is just a hop neuron... different dna row' (10-26 05:12). Each hop calls the write run, which writes the receipt row into R1's sheet. His words 10-28: 'if physics writes the brain will not be able to see or observe what happened,, anything the brain cannot see is a step the brain cannot build upon... run receipt is just the order of the main run plus the hops, so it's just recorded in the run data sheet as a row and columns, then read and written by the brain'.
The write run lays one row of R1's sheet per hop.
The path of gates and shards: a pointer to the run, never the run again (10-23 P2). Rows and columns of the run data sheet, written by the write run (his words 10-28).

His words 10-28: 'born inline is mechanical intelligence perspective... meaning missing neuron = missing step ... new neuron must be born such that the next step can be completed.... traverse back and retry.... has to do with a failed cell on the run data sheet, if the new step, or the next step fails to provide the run data sheet with data then the run must be re ran via different substitution theory or using a different formula, via process of elimination theory ... meaning there is a check back or even step back to a run that had a choice ... the failed choice is remembered from the time line and eliminated'.
A copy run the ending shard excites; the trigger writes nothing itself (10-26 03:59). It lays run_memory(1, receipt, user) on 66.s118 and the run_sheet rows inside it (his v4 shape).
By a trigger hop, never a sweep (10-23 P3 B1). One row: the clock reading, the receipt pointer, a couple of key words (10-16 06:40). Then it stops (10-26 03:50).
10-26 03:50: when the run's data table is complete the run can populate and finish its larger formulas.
10-23 P3 B2. On a fresh brain nothing is bound to define yet; the material is the sheet: the compiled definitions of 64 and 66 and the labeled guess for 65.
10-23 P5-9 B1. Not balanced: step back to the decision that picked this path and take another row; the failed try stays in memory marked wrong (10-22 rev17; his words 10-28).

His words 10-28: 'before a run answers define? back to the user, it askes the sixth why define? and the sixth replies your run data sheet at location x,y,z is missing cells... or it calls to the sixth or the guessing brain for a balance/progression check'.

The say run: the reply as a tree of arrays, each pick opening the next (10-23 P3 B2); the brain chooses what it wants to say (10-27 03:52); no sentence drawn here on purpose (10-27 04:07). 10-26 05:12: the say key = the metadata on what leaves (lane 0).
10-23 P3 B2: just gate numbers, maybe head data.

His words 10-28: 'all guesses in an output are labeled and asked correct?/incorrect?/progression?/ degression? <-- that answer is what helps adjust the weights and build the confidence to change a guess into a belief'.
10-25 msg 41: run output to sixth.
His words 10-28. 10-23 P5-9 B1: taught is not believed; belief from memory, source trust, supporting knowledge.

Born inline when a gate is missing (missing neuron = missing step). Step back to a run that had a choice when a cell fails; the failed choice is remembered from the timeline and eliminated; rerun by a different substitution or formula. Drawn: lane 3 and lane 6.

'if physics writes the brain will not be able to see or observe what happened... run receipt is just the order of the main run plus the hops, so it's just recorded in the run data sheet as a row and columns'. Drawn: lane 3.
The question explained in lane 0 (the memory table shape). His own typing of 10-27 01:17 is the answer the drawing follows.
'once the variables are determined then that row cannot live in the main run... thus a new neuron must be born'. Drawn: lane 5 (70) and lane 2 (67, 68, 69).
Drawn: lane 2 (the long runs and the formula neurons born), lane 5b (the jumps).

'every turn even define : who or learn : who or meaning : who requires all the things in order to be done correct... give the brain the ability to build it all through systems or processes it builds step by step by step inside the first run'. Drawn: lane 13 and the inside of every step (KEY).
Drawn: lane 5 (worked), lane 10 (correct?), lane 11.
His guesses for its columns: what is this data in perspective to this run, where does it belong, what does it solve, who said it, when, why, what modifiers. Drawn: lane 0 (the key shape), lanes 4, 6.

The example on this line: for who, WordNet sent 'a United Nations agency' (the WHO), Webster 'an interrogative pronoun, later a relative pronoun', Merriam-Webster 'what or which person or persons' and 'the person or persons that: whoever'. The earlier build kept only the words two sources shared and dropped the rest, and on 10-23 P4 B1 he said 'the diffs are kind of dropped or scattered and the similars are kept. But I don't know that we're getting a good, valid definition that way... if the definitions are wrong, then the description of the meaning is wrong'. The drawing keeps every source's line as its own row, kept apart by source, and lets the compile lay relationship rows from them; what the compile DROPS, if anything, and what counts as 'similar' (the same gates? the same relationships?) is the open part.
His guesses listed in lane 0; which are needed is found as the brain grows.
10-23 P4: 'in order to have the definitions, you have to have 500 or 1,000 words that you don't have meanings for'. The drawing stops one level down.
His words 10-28: 'you have to take in account variables and modifiers sometimes in this aspect such to get the full use of a formula in any one context'.
His words 10-28. The core drawn here is 63 and is a reading.
His words 10-28 name all three.

The born run, excited by the no-gate condition at 64 (10-20 01:22). Arrived from 64, goes on to 4 (CREATE); spawn column: the ask run (51) for the newborn's sources (10-23 P4). It declares on R1's sheet the cell gate.64 and its own sheet: value, text, reply.
His words 10-28 (the say key): the metadata that travels with the script to mother and back with the response, so the return fills the right cell of the right run.

The build neuron: 'the last build word was the build neuron... routing information for the mother... build neuron = routing to sql prompt' (10-26 03:50). Its row, picked by before (10 ;) and no remainder, is a build row because of how before and remainder are set, not by counting. No remainder: this shard ends R2 and carries R2's memory node. The build neuron ends every born run, so it gains one memory node per born run (his words 10-28).
The port the run hits to leave: the product and the key go on the brain > mother mailbox. 10-23 msg 1: output to sources is a dna row and trigger to port.

10-19 23:03: the statement as the product of the run. 10-24 msg 36: the run data sheet produces the exact code that sql needs to run as output the same way that it forms human sentences; given to the mother to route to the sql prompt.
10-24 msg 36; 10-26 03:50: each return fills its spot. The key says which run and which cell. An error is not an end (10-27 03:52).
R2's memory row on the shard that ended it, with its sheet inside. Cells declared by the triggers that tripped (10-26 03:50).
One row per run that ends (10-16 06:40).
The write run: excited by the value neuron's call; writes value = 64 into R2's sheet (10-26 03:59: the trigger just triggers that run, often used with the copy run, and cut run).

His words 10-28: 'it's done by way of the first time it works, and is correct'; in context: 'when it works and is correct the graph will have meanings of its own, the graph shape of runs will start to show us more information'. [reading] 'works' = the next step of the run that needed it completed; 'correct' grows with the user's correct/incorrect and the sixth's observation (lanes 10, 11).

His words 10-28: 'it triggers a decide formula run that decides what the formula is, then writes it in that runs data sheet'. It reads R2's receipt (46), compares (55) the hits against the run's input to find which hits carried the variable (the value neuron's shards), and the write run (43) writes the formula into R2's sheet cell formula: the receipt with the holes marked.
Which hits are the variables: the ones whose value came from the sheet, not from the line.
Writes cell formula into R2's memory node.

His words 10-28: 'a long run has an end, that run basically = a specific formula sometimes but the variables are already filled in. determining the formula neuron is figuring out what the variables of the formula is... once the variables are determined then that row cannot live in the main run because it doesn't match the run receipt of that run... thus a new neuron must be born, that is relationally matched to that long run, but can be used with different variables on other runs also.... you have to take in account variables and modifiers'. Born by the born run (the long way, the last time: [reading] its own birth has no formula yet). Its row: arrived from born (41), goes on to the value neuron (18) with a new shard per run; calls the substitution run (54).

The pointer circles back to the memory of the long run (his words 10-28: 'on the pointer the circle is back to the memory of the run ... or maybe the run data sheet'). The standing question SQ3 finds it next time: 'do I have a formula that is proven to try first'.

His words 10-28: 'through back population the triggers or calls or jumps or hops from a run create table (value) would have to show the substitution run and the write run writing the value, then the trigger of the substitution run copying into the substitution run so that you can then skip the long run and use the formula neuron'. 10-23 P5-9: back population is the application of a newly understood process to the other things it fits.
His words 10-28: 'it all circles back to the standing questions... do I have a formula that is proven to try first.... this is the step at the beginning that skips the long run'.
If no formula were born yet, the shortcut path would replay the long run from this memory (his words 10-28: 'the shortcut path if the variable formula path is not found yet').
The same born neuron, a new shard for this run: arrived from 65. Every run begins with the three questions (his words 10-28), so it goes on to 67 (know). Spawns the ask run (51).
The question is a jump now: the formula neuron born in lane 2, variables plugged in.
His words 10-28: 'uses the variable formula path or the shortcut path if the variable formula path is not found yet'.

The same shard 4.s122 the long run wrote, now carrying the jump laid by back population: the long run is skipped. 10-08: 'if I know where I am standing I can hop to any point in my brain in one step... all the work was done at learning, not at runtime'.
The formula neuron born after R2. Goes on to the value neuron; calls the substitution run.
A different shard in the value neuron for each new run (his words 10-28): s271 for R4. Its call: the write run writes the value variable, 65, into R4's sheet.
Writes value = 65 into R4's sheet cell value ('the formula shortcut is just to the data sheet writing the value variable', his words 10-28).

'substitution run grabbing that value and plugging it into the run data sheet so a new memory node can be made or a new neuron can be made' (his words 10-28). Its call: the copy run copies the formula (R2's sheet cell formula, the receipt with the holes) into this run's sheet; the holes are filled with cell value.
Copies R2.sheet.formula into R4's sheet cell text ('the trigger of the substitution run copying into the substitution run', his words 10-28).
The build neuron again, a new shard for R4: it ends the run, so it carries another memory node. The build neuron now holds memory nodes for R2, R4, ...
The port: the product and the key (R4 | reply | 40 | t) go to mother.
A separate memory node on a separate ending shard of the same neuron 40, with its own sheet inside (his words 10-28). 10 hits instead of 99.
The same born neuron, a new shard for this run: arrived from 66. Every run begins with the three questions (his words 10-28), so it goes on to 67 (know). Spawns the ask run (51).
The question is a jump now: the formula neuron born in lane 2, variables plugged in.
His words 10-28: 'uses the variable formula path or the shortcut path if the variable formula path is not found yet'.

The same shard 4.s122 the long run wrote, now carrying the jump laid by back population: the long run is skipped. 10-08: 'if I know where I am standing I can hop to any point in my brain in one step... all the work was done at learning, not at runtime'.
The formula neuron born after R2. Goes on to the value neuron; calls the substitution run.
A different shard in the value neuron for each new run (his words 10-28): s281 for R6. Its call: the write run writes the value variable, 66, into R6's sheet.
Writes value = 66 into R6's sheet cell value ('the formula shortcut is just to the data sheet writing the value variable', his words 10-28).

'substitution run grabbing that value and plugging it into the run data sheet so a new memory node can be made or a new neuron can be made' (his words 10-28). Its call: the copy run copies the formula (R2's sheet cell formula, the receipt with the holes) into this run's sheet; the holes are filled with cell value.
Copies R2.sheet.formula into R6's sheet cell text ('the trigger of the substitution run copying into the substitution run', his words 10-28).
The build neuron again, a new shard for R6: it ends the run, so it carries another memory node. The build neuron now holds memory nodes for R2, R6, ...
The port: the product and the key (R6 | reply | 40 | t) go to mother.
A separate memory node on a separate ending shard of the same neuron 40, with its own sheet inside (his words 10-28). 10 hits instead of 99.

The ask run, spawned by the born run. Declares its own sheet: one cell per source and compile; declares on R1's sheet the cell def.64. Assembles the ask from the encoder's label of the newborn and goes on to 60 (out). The run names the sources; mother carries the ask to each inbox and decides nothing (10-23 P2; 10-23 01:28).
The key travels to each source and back with each answer (his words 10-28).

The source run's own sheet: a cell per source, filled by each return; when no declared cell is empty the compile runs (10-26 03:50). Counts are the real lines in the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json).
